clue.text: Gauge apple-splitting speed? We’ll see

blocks.note: to gauge how fast something goes is to time it
William Tell, the Swiss folk hero, split an apple on his son's head with a crossbow bolt; Will is short for William
surface padding: says what is being gauged, adding no letters

explanation.surface: A question about measuring how fast an apple is split, followed by a non-committal shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'time Will Tell', that is, gauge the speed of the apple-splitter; 'speed' just tells you what is being timed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said when an outcome cannot yet be known and only waiting will reveal it, just as 'we'll see' is.

clue.text: Some aircraft skip prescribed courses

blocks.note: to trip is to skip lightly along
lanes are set routes, as on a running track or a shipping route

explanation.surface: Some planes miss the flight paths laid down for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplanes are early aeroplanes with three stacked wings, such as the Fokker Dr.I, so they are a type of flying machine.

clue.text: He experimented with light Jiffy bag

blocks.note: a mo, short for moment, is a jiffy
to bag something is to net it

explanation.surface: Someone tried out a lightweight padded envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jiffy bag is a British brand of padded envelope; the brand name is split, and 'light' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet, the Impressionist painter, studied how changing daylight altered scenes such as haystacks and Rouen Cathedral.

clue.text: Fare given out with a taste of wine?

definitions.text: Fare given out with a taste of wine?
definitions.note: the whole clue describes the communion bread

indicators.note: a mere taste is the smallest first portion, so only the opening letter is used
things given out are distributed and scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food handed out alongside a sip of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: at Holy Communion the host is handed out to worshippers along with a sip of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin disc of unleavened bread given at the Eucharist alongside the consecrated wine is called a communion host.

clue.text: The most arrogant way is through divination

indicators.note: one thing passing through another sits inside it

blocks.note: the start of a lot, which is drawn to decide things by chance
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
something that is somewhere lies there
the rest of the lot

explanation.surface: The haughtiest approach is to foretell the future.
explanation.walkthrough: Casting or drawing lots is an ancient method of divination; RD+LIES goes through LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means haughty and imperious, like a lord, so its superlative describes the most arrogant.

clue.text: Classy brace of prizes being put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from the bottom upward

blocks.note: a brace is two, and two prizes are a reward and a pot (a trophy)

explanation.surface: A smart pair of trophies being displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the highest social class or top quality, as the best things are kept in the uppermost drawer.

clue.text: Cooperative meetings adult is running out of pride?

definitions.note: a pride is a group of the animals named by the plural answer

indicators.note: running out of something means no longer having it, so those letters go

blocks.note: liaisons are meetings for working together
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up abandoning cooperative gatherings because their self-respect has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like self-respect, but it is the collective noun for a group of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is the collective noun for a group of these big cats, so the plural animals make up one.

clue.text: Proposes to have train sign erected for one local game

indicators.note: in a down entry, erecting means standing the letters up from the bottom
taking the place of one, the Roman numeral, means swapping that letter out

blocks.note: to propose an offer is to bid
to rail is to travel by train
Libra is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A railway sign put up for a regional sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' means a British pub, which is a local; bar billiards is a pub table game. The reversed letters replace the I in BIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar billiards is a table game played in pubs, and a pub is a local, so it is a game of the local.

clue.text: Right to go after a Klingon?

definitions.note: a Klingon is one example, hence the question mark

blocks.note: taken as written
a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone asserting a right to pursue a Star Trek warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go after' tells you the right comes after A; the definition is the last two words, the A doing double duty only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Klingons are a warlike extraterrestrial race in Star Trek, so one of them is an example of a being from another world.

clue.text: Rocket from Toto, perhaps, unlikely to go up

blocks.note: Toto Wolff runs a Formula One team, so he exemplifies F1, read here as the letters F and I
a rocket is a severe telling-off, which is a reproof

explanation.surface: A dog from Oz fires a rocket that will never leave the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Toto suggests Dorothy's dog, but here it is Toto Wolff, the Mercedes Formula One boss; 'from' puts the telling-off after F1, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resists burning will not go up in flames, so it is unlikely to go up in the sense of catching fire.

clue.text: Ritual inversion affecting police uniform?

indicators.note: an inversion turns order upside down, here swapping the words around

blocks.note: the dress of the police force, a habit being a distinctive costume

explanation.surface: A ceremonial swap that changes the police's dress code.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal works on whole words, not letters: 'habit of force' becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is something done routinely out of custom, and doing it automatically because of routine is the idiom here.

clue.text: Bye … one farewell leads to another – logic for two parties!

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front ends, so only their opening letters are wanted

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a bye
the Roman numeral for one
'later!' is an informal way of saying goodbye
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A chain of goodbyes, one prompting the next, presented as a triumphant bit of two-sided reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter without being hit, recorded as B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilateral agreement or arrangement involves two sides, so the word describes something done by or for two parties.

clue.text: Tubing towards surface, trains (Métro) appearing at set intervals

indicators.note: letters that show up at fixed spacing are every other one, skipping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Paris underground trains turn up at regular intervals through their tunnels.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from the second letter of 'trains' and take every other one through 'Métro', the accent ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing and building services a riser is a vertical pipe carrying water or gas upward toward the floors above.

clue.text: Light given to modern-day soldiers

blocks.note: to light on something is to land on it
a present given to someone is one for them
CE, Common Era, is the dating label for the present era

explanation.surface: Illumination being supplied to today's army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun meaning illumination, but it is the verb meaning to alight or settle.
explanation.definitionFit: A land force is an army fighting on the ground, and its troops collectively are soldiers.

clue.text: Delicate condition recurring – great pain, but not as bad

indicators.note: something recurring comes back round, so the letters run backwards
'not' tells us to drop the letters spelt by the word as
something bad is spoiled, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: if introduces a condition
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sensitive medical state that keeps coming back, with great pain that is not quite as severe.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both As from GREAT PAIN, leaving GRETPIN, then jumble it after the reversed IF.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes very fine, light control such as the touch of a hand's extremity, hence delicate.

clue.text: Check person on board’s sacking female risk-taker

indicators.note: sacking someone removes them, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a surfer stands on a board
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Check whether a board member is firing a woman who takes risks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person on board' suggests a company director, but it is someone riding waves.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer of insurers takes on part of other insurance companies' liabilities, so it accepts risk.

clue.text: With gap, it wouldn’t be!

definitions.note: the whole clue describes something complete

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: A wry remark that something with a gap in it could not be complete.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay at once: the letters spell 'with a gap', and a thing with a gap would not be complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire has no part missing, so anything with a gap in it fails to be complete.

clue.text: Those commanding such a view from NW8 high-rise?

blocks.note: surface padding: frames the scene, adding no letters
a tall building looks out over what is below it
Lord's cricket ground is in the London postcode district NW8

explanation.surface: Residents of a London tower block who enjoy a commanding view.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's great cricket ground, in St John's Wood, NW8; a tower there looks out over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers holding supreme power over others, so they are those in command.

clue.text: Dramatist written about in one’s biography

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
'about' signals turning round, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A playwright is discussed in someone's life story.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading backwards through oNE'S BIography gives the Norwegian playwright IBSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen wrote plays such as A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler, so he is a dramatist.

clue.text: Insert line after edits

indicators.note: an editor rearranges and reworks text, so the following words are rewritten in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction to put a line in once the edits are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insert' is a noun here, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An interleaf is an extra page bound between the regular pages of a book, a kind of inserted sheet.

clue.text: Discharged earth

definitions.note: the whole clue describes soil thrown up into a raised line

blocks.note: rid means freed of or cleared
Ge, or Gaia, is the Greek personification of the earth

explanation.walkthrough: A plough throws earth out to one side, and that discharged soil builds up into a long raised strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised strip of soil turned up between furrows by ploughing is the long narrow mound formed from that thrown-out ground.

clue.text: You got me through bridgehead unnoticed

indicators.note: running through the following words, the letters are found inside them

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A soldier admits sneaking past the enemy's forward position without being spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial admissions of ignorance, said when someone asks a question you cannot answer.

clue.text: Evergreen old Duke Elgar will without delay set off on cycle

indicators.note: going round a cycle moves the front of the sequence round to the back

blocks.note: ASAP is as soon as possible
O is the abbreviation for old
D is the abbreviation for duke
Elgar is the setter, who would say 'I will' as I'LL

explanation.surface: The old Duke's will is read out at once, with Elgar setting off on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar is the composer, but also the setter's own pen name, so 'Elgar will' is his 'I'll'. Take ASAP+O+D+ILL and move the opening A to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapodilla is a tropical American tree that keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Pan freshly filled with uncooked shellfish

indicators.note: a new filling replaces the old one, so the middle is swapped for something else

blocks.note: taken as written
raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: A frying pan newly loaded with raw seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in the middle of PAN is replaced by RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns are small edible crustaceans, and crustaceans of that kind are commonly called shellfish.

clue.text: Turf out of playing area, upset at recording

indicators.note: upsetting a thing turns it over, so in a down entry the letters run upward

blocks.note: at and to both mark direction, as in throwing at or to someone
vid is informal for a video recording

explanation.surface: Someone being thrown off the pitch, annoyed at being filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turf out' looks like a verb meaning to evict, but the definition is a noun: a piece of turf out of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A divot is the chunk of grass and soil gouged out of a golf course or pitch by a club or a hoof.

clue.text: I go off rounds in Yemen city hospitals

indicators.note: something that comes round turns back on itself, so the preceding pair is read backwards
'in' places one group of letters inside the following city name

blocks.note: taken as written
to go off, as food does, is to rot
Sanaa is the capital of Yemen

explanation.surface: A doctor deteriorating while doing ward rounds in a Yemeni hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' suggests doctors' ward rounds, but here it turns the first pair back to front; Yemen's capital is spelt with a double A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria, a Latin plural, are institutions for treating long-term illness or convalescence, a kind of hospital.

clue.text: Musician never discussed covers

indicators.note: the outer words cover, or conceal, letters within them

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A performer whose cover versions are never talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like the songs a musician records, but it says the next words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi composed operas such as Aida and La Traviata, so he was a musician.

clue.text: Consult A&E?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase describing an action

blocks.note: first meaning: talk things over and share views with someone
second meaning: A and E are musical notes, set side by side for comparison

explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital casualty department, Accident and Emergency, which makes 'consult' sound medical; here A and E are two notes of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare notes is an idiom for exchanging information and opinions, which is what consulting someone involves.
